what_happened: The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path curved right, but after handoff the policy steered left across the wide multi-lane road, ending up 13 m from the recorded path. At 8.8 s it was off the drivable area, near actor 70. The input also flags an at-fault collision at that moment, but the metrics table shows no collision, so leaving the road is the main failure.

On a straight multi-lane highway, after handoff the policy steered right toward the next lane (orange plan headed toward car 4), even though the human had stayed in lane. The ego's front then hit car 3, which was driving alongside in that right lane, at about 5.8 m/s.

The ego was in slow highway traffic with a clear gap ahead. After the policy took over at 4.7 s, it planned and steered left, away from the recorded path, even though the route command switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT. It crossed the left lane edge into the concrete median barrier and was offroad by 7.0 s, 3.4 m from where the human drove.

On the multi-lane highway, the human drove on in its lane and then moved left (the command changed to LEFT). The policy instead braked hard (21→8 m/s), which let semi-truck 5 in the lane to the right pull ahead of it. It then steered right into the truck's lane, and its front hit the side of the truck at 8.0 s, about 4.7 m off the recorded path.

The road curved to the right and the command was RIGHT, but after handoff the ego kept heading straight and then steered left. It crossed the lanes toward the left road edge and sidewalk, ending about 12 m from the human path while braking from 17 to 7 m/s. As it left the road, actor 32, which was driving along the lanes, made side contact with it.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the policy took over and planned an unprompted lane change to the right, away from the recorded path that kept the lane. It cut into the adjacent right lane and its front hit actor 3, which was driving alongside, at about 6.6 m/s.

Shortly after handoff, the policy planned a leftward path even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. It drifted across the left lanes while slowing from about 18 to 11 m/s and ran onto the planted median at 7.1s, about 7 m from the recorded trajectory. No other actor was involved, and the camera view looked clean before the drift.

The road curves left (the command switches to LEFT). The ego slowed from about 23 to 16 m/s but kept heading straight instead of following the curve. It ran off the right edge onto the shoulder or sidewalk by the fence, about 2.5 m from the recorded path. No other actors were involved, and the camera view stayed clean before the failure.

After the 4.7 s handoff, the route command switched to RIGHT and the planned path bent right toward the recorded lane. Instead, the ego slowed from about 29 to 20 m/s while drifting left across the yellow edge line, ending about 2.2 m off the recorded trajectory, off the road and into the vegetation on the left at 6.7 s. There were no actors nearby and the camera view looked fine until the departure, so the policy's steering caused this.

Shortly after the 4.7 s handoff, on a multi-lane highway with the route command STRAIGHT, the policy began an unprompted lane change to the right toward the gap behind actor 4. Its front corner hit actor 3, which was driving alongside in the right lane, at 6.4 s at about 5.7 m/s, 1.6 m off the recorded human path.

On a straight multi-lane freeway with the command STRAIGHT, then LEFT at 6.4 s, the policy took over at 4.7 s and planned a lane change to the right toward actor 4's lane. It angled across the lane line and its front hit actor 3, which was driving alongside in the right lane, even though the actor ahead in its own lane was still about 12 m away.

After the policy took over at 4.5 s, the ego kept going straight at about 23 m/s down to 16 m/s while the road curved left, and the route command switched to LEFT. It drifted about 2.5 m right of the recorded human path and onto the right shoulder, past the drivable boundary, at 6.6 s. No other actor was involved.

With no actors nearby, the ego (about 23 m/s, slowing to 16 m/s) failed to follow the road's leftward curve and drifted over the right edge line onto the shoulder and dirt by the fence, about 2.7 m off the human path. Its planned path headed right instead of following the lane.

After the 4.7 s handoff, the ego was in slow highway traffic at about 5 m/s. Instead of following the route straight and then right, it steered left out of its lane toward the median barrier, while the recorded path stayed to the right. By 7.0 s it was about 3.5 m off the recorded path and off the drivable area at the left edge. The camera was clean at 5–6 s and showed the barrier clearly, so a broken render doesn't explain the mistake.

On a busy multi-lane highway, the policy took over at 4.7 s at about 4.5 m/s. The route said RIGHT and the recorded path angled right, but the ego steered left across the lanes and ended up offroad at 7.0 s, 3.5 m off the recorded path and heading toward the left barrier. The camera view at 5–6 s was clean enough to drive on, and the collision metrics in the table stay at 0, so the failure is the ego leaving the road by its own steering.

After the policy took over at 4.7 s on the highway, the ego's planned path veered right, off the route, toward the next lane. It started changing lanes to the right at about 6.5 m/s and drove its front into actor 3, which was in that lane just ahead and to the right. The route command said STRAIGHT and then LEFT, and nothing in front forced a lane change, because the lead car was still about 16 m ahead.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy took over at 4.7 s and started a lane change to the right. The recorded human path stayed in the current lane. At 6.5 s the ego's front hit actor 3, which was driving next to it in the right lane, about 1.7 m from where the human drove.

The route command switched to RIGHT and the recorded path moved right, but the ego kept heading slightly left. It slowed from about 28 to 19 m/s and drifted onto the yellow left edge line by the guardrail, where it went offroad about 2 m from the human's path. No other actors were close.

After handoff at 4.7 s, the ego braked from about 29 to 19.5 m/s but drifted left instead of following the route, which bore right (the command changed to RIGHT). By 6.8 s it had crossed the yellow left edge line onto the left shoulder, about 2.4 m off the recorded path. The camera view was clean before the drift, so this is the policy's steering error.
